english: Let $E$ be the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}+y^{2}=1$ and let $A$ be the point $(-2,0)$. For a point $P$ on the parabola $y^{2}=4x$, the line $AP$ meets $E$ again at the point $Q$. As $P$ varies over the parabola, the least value of the abscissa of $Q$ is
hindi: माना कि $E$ दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}+y^{2}=1$ है तथा $A$ बिन्दु $(-2,0)$ है। परवलय $y^{2}=4x$ पर स्थित किसी बिन्दु $P$ के लिए, रेखा $AP$ दीर्घवृत्त $E$ को पुनः बिन्दु $Q$ पर मिलती है। जब $P$ परवलय पर गति करता है, तब $Q$ के भुज का न्यूनतम मान है
solution_full: The ellipse is $\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{1}=1$, so its points are $Q(2\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$, and $A(-2,0)$ corresponds to $\theta=\pi$. The point $Q$ is the second intersection, so $\theta\neq\pi$.

A point of the parabola $y^{2}=4x$ is $P(t^{2},2t)$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$. Since $t^{2}\geq 0>-2$, the line $AP$ is never vertical, so it is never the tangent $x=-2$ at $A$ and always meets $E$ at a second point.
By AM-GM, $t^{2}+2\geq 2\sqrt{2}\,|t|$, so $|T|\leq\dfrac{4|t|}{2\sqrt{2}|t|}=\sqrt{2}$ for $t\neq0$ (and $T=0$ for $t=0$). Hence $0\leq T^{2}\leq 2$, and $T^{2}=2$ exactly when $t^{2}=2$.
The abscissa of $Q$ is $x_{Q}=2\cos\theta=2\cdot\dfrac{1-T^{2}}{1+T^{2}}=2\left(\dfrac{2}{1+T^{2}}-1\right)$, which is a decreasing function of $T^{2}$.

So $x_{Q}$ is least when $T^{2}=2$: $x_{Q}=2\cdot\dfrac{1-2}{1+2}=-\dfrac{2}{3}$. This is attained for $P(2,\pm2\sqrt{2})$, when $Q=\left(-\dfrac{2}{3},\pm\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\right)$; check: $\dfrac{4/9}{4}+\dfrac{8}{9}=1$.
originality_note: New: the second intersection of the line from the left vertex of an ellipse through a point of a parabola; the half-angle tan(theta/2) of the eccentric angle equals twice the slope, and the parabola's parameter enters through 4t/(t^2+2), maximised by AM-GM (way 5, a new combination where the link is the half-angle slope). Closest known: 'chord through a vertex of an ellipse with slope m meets it again at ...' exercises and maximum of a slope from a fixed point to a parabola. Different because: the extreme position of Q is controlled by the parabola, and the answer needs the monotonic dependence of 2cos(theta) on tan^2(theta/2).

concept_use.Parametric coordinates for parabola: P is taken as (t^2, 2t), so the slope of AP is 2t/(t^2+2) and its range is found by AM-GM in t.
concept_use.Parametric coordinates for Ellipse: Q is taken as (2cos(theta), sin(theta)); the slope of AQ is (1/2)tan(theta/2), and x_Q = 2cos(theta) is written in tan(theta/2).

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve and point is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and checked by an independent numerical route, is unique and matches the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that AP is never the tangent x=-2 at A (so Q exists for every P), that the least value is attained (at t^2=2), and that the four options are distinct negative fractions with only (C) correct as planned. Changed: removed 'other than its vertex' (for P at the vertex, Q=(2,0) is still defined and does not affect the minimum).
key_step: Linking the slope of AQ to tan(theta/2) of the eccentric angle, then bounding 4t/(t^2+2) by AM-GM and using that 2cos(theta) decreases in tan^2(theta/2).
justification: Two parametric descriptions must be linked through the half-angle slope and then an extremum found; neither step is a single formula, and the monotonicity argument is easy to get backwards. Comparable to 2025-P2-Q7 (L3), which links ellipse points to angles, and above the routine parametric chain of 2026-P2-Q2 (L2).
